title: Hilbert-Series Lower Bound on Solving Degree
summary: For the cipher-modeling polynomial systems, it remains to prove or refute whether solving degree is at least the first non-positive-coefficient index of the Hilbert series.

formal_statement.body: For the constructed overdefined polynomial systems used to model Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit, prove or refute that the solving degree is at least the index of the first non-positive coefficient in the corresponding Hilbert series $S_{m,n}(z)$. [S1] The question concerns the conjectured lower bound in the setting where the Hilbert series can upper-bound the solving degree when syzygies are mainly trivial, while many non-trivial syzygies may require computation at a larger degree. [S1]

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis via overdefined polynomial systems modeling Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit.
parameters: m and n: parameters indexing the Hilbert series
z: variable of the Hilbert series
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that the solving degree is lower-bounded by the index of the first non-positive coefficient in the corresponding Hilbert series.

citations.label: Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents the lower bound as a conjecture. It motivates the conjecture by contrasting mainly trivial syzygies, for which the Hilbert series can upper-bound solving degree, with non-trivial syzygies that may require computation at a larger degree.
citation_labels: Fukang Liu et al., Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit
